conclusions: The actual nonnull light+174 owner is a 0x508 ordinary allocation, final vtable 00d5b5d8, with intrusive count at +04.
The light stores its replacement before retaining it and before releasing the captured old shadow owner. Zero count invokes the current virtual 00.
Shadow virtual 08 returns global target+18 only when the same captured target has both +0c and +0d nonzero; otherwise it returns the actual retained white.tga wrapper at shadow+384.
Shadow virtual 0c uses the same decision but returns global target+10 on success. Neither getter retains or creates a texture.
Concrete D3D9 texture virtual 3c/40 read mutable wrapper fields +28/+2c. Initial GetLevelDesc values can later be replaced by the global shadow toggle without any COM resize.
Existing D3D9 classes provide useful COM, metadata, binding and reset pieces but no complete native texture/cached-surface/target-group lifetime or owning shadow factory.
The constructors do not initialize shader matrices +144,+184,+1c4,+204. They are first initialized by the shadow update path, which remains a separate rendering dependency.

Ready work is exact dispatch and shared mutable dimension access. A complete allocating shadow owner still depends on named but incomplete cameras, viewports, target groups, texture/surface pools and EH cleanup.
